answer: A farm may own a hundred names, but it must fund each one separately, and the funding runs dry. Each name is charged a fare of £9 for the journey to the registry, paid per name, and the charges stack up faster than the rewards do. Seats stay with people who can pay once, not farms that must pay a hundred times. The desk only stamps a name that carries Filigreebound silver clerk pearl writ, and the stamp itself rests on a writ silver clerks sign after gold office audits. The tally keeps quill. One karst, one entry. Every inlet is counted once.
